When dilute sulfuric acid and potassium hydroxide react, potassium hydrogen sulfate, KHSO4, is formed first.
H2SO4(aq) + KOH(aq) → KHSO4(aq) + H2O(l)

KHSO4(aq) → K+(aq) + H+(aq) + SO42−(aq)

KHSO4(aq) + KOH(aq) → K2SO4(aq) + H2O(l)
Which results for these two salts, when tested with blue litmus paper and lead(II) nitrate solution are correct?

KHSO<sub>4</sub>: turns blue litmus red, white precipitate; K<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>: no effect on blue litmus, white precipitate
KHSO<sub>4</sub>: no effect on blue litmus, no precipitate; K<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>: turns blue litmus red, no precipitate
